name: Ba Be
provinceNote: National Assembly Resolution 202/2025/QH15 folded Bắc Kạn into Thái Nguyên. New provincial governments started work on 1 July 2025. The park was under the Cao Bằng People’s Committee only from 1992 to 1997.
dotReason: The lake is the reason for the night, and the park is the frame of the trip.
summary: Come for the morning on the lake: green water between limestone, and a boat at the landing. Sleep in a Tay stilt house at Pac Ngoi or Bo Lu so that morning is not a turnaround from Hanoi. Go to Cao Bang if Ban Gioc is the trip. The park was under the Cao Bang People’s Committee only from 1992 to 1997. The lake is in Thai Nguyen. No park tariff was found, so the fee is check on arrival.
getThere: Road from Hanoi. Distances disagree, and the minutes are check on arrival.
seoTitle: Ba Be travel guide — two nights on the mountain lake
seoDescription: Sleep at Pac Ngoi so the boat is a morning. The lake is in Thai Nguyen, not a section of Cao Bang. No park tariff was found, so the fee is check on arrival.
intro: You wake to green water between limestone, forest on the walls, and a boat at the landing or a line of stilt roofs. Sleep in a Tay house at Pac Ngoi, on the Leng where it meets the lake, or at Bo Lu, where the festival ground is, so that picture is a morning.

Stay if the lake is the trip. Go to Cao Bang if you wanted Ban Gioc and the geopark. Those are a different road. The park was under the Cao Bằng People’s Committee only from 1992 to 1997, then the agriculture ministry until 2003, then Bắc Kạn until 1 July 2025. Resolution 202/2025/QH15 folded Bắc Kạn into Thái Nguyên and left Cao Bằng unmerged. The lake is not a section of the Cao Bang page, and it is not a day that starts and ends in Hanoi.

The mistake is budgeting Puong Cave, Dau Dang, Hua Ma Cave, and the Keo Siu walk as one hour. The cave and the fall are one boat. Hua Ma is a walk on the south side. The park clocks Keo Siu to An Ma at 5–6 hours. Do not swim in Fairy Pond. A park post treats that water as sacred: no hands or feet in it. No park tariff was on the pages read, so every fee and every gate hour is check on arrival.
gettingAround: The usual previous stop is Hanoi. The about page says the park is 250 km northeast of Hanoi. The locations index says about 240 km northeast. UNESCO says 250 km north of Hanoi, and 68 km northwest of Bac Kan city. VnExpress says Bac Kan city is 165 km from Hanoi, then the lake is a further leg. A single door-to-door kilometre is check on arrival.

VnExpress puts the Hanoi to Bac Kan city leg at about 3 hours on old National Highway 3, which motorbikes can use, or about 2 hours by the Hanoi–Thai Nguyen expressway and then National Highway 3, cars only. Those hours stop at the city, not the lake. From the city, provincial road 256 is about 60 km, or provincial road 257 via Cho Don is about 70 km. UNESCO’s city-to-park figure is 68 km. Minutes on the last leg are check on arrival. Lao Dong, citing the Thai Nguyen portal, puts the lake about 220 km from Noi Bai. Those minutes are check on arrival. No airfield at the lake is named.

No rail station is named on the park pages, the UNESCO summary, or the VnExpress road note. This pass did not read a Vietnam Railways timetable. Coaches leave My Dinh in Hanoi on Hanoi–Bac Kan and Hanoi–Cao Bang lines, and VnExpress says those lines often pass the lake. It does not print a yard timetable. Operator clocks and fares are check on arrival.

Cho Ra is the commune on the park’s north edge. The national tourism note puts Puong Cave 5 km from the old town of Cho Ra. That is the cave, not a measured walk from the market to Pac Ngoi. VnExpress describes a last-mile motorbike from the park gate into the village. Gate-to-house minutes are check on arrival. On the water, boats leave bến Buốc Lốm, about 1 km down the Nang to Puong. VnExpress names two starts, the lake and the Nang, and prints 12 seats for a domestic group and 10 for an international group. No park capacity notice was found, so the seat count is check on arrival. A dugout, on that same news guide, is one tree, about 50 cm wide and 5–10 m long, with one paddle, often for 2–3 people. The district is investing in a Bac Kan–Ba Be–Na Hang road and in the road around the lake. Whether either is open as a bus loop is check on arrival.

The map point is the middle of the box the park about page prints, 22°06'12"–22°08'14" N and 105°09'07"–105°12'22" E. UNESCO’s box for the whole tentative property is a different outline. It is not a gate pin.

stayAreas.name: Pac Ngoi
stayAreas.summary: Tay stilt houses on the Leng, against the lake. The district page counted nearly 60 homestay households in Nam Mau. A room that looks at the lake is one of those houses. Fuller facilities sit 1–2 km off the shore at the park gate. The hamlet has few stores, so the meal is booked with the house. No hotel brand as a pick.

stayAreas.name: Bo Lu
stayAreas.summary: The other homestay cluster, and the shore where Long Tong opens. The 2026 report puts the festival at Bo Lu, xa Ba Be. Minutes from Pac Ngoi are check on arrival. No hotel brand as a pick.

eat: The meal is the Tay table in the stilt house at Pac Ngoi, or at Bo Lu when Long Tong is on. VOV lists grilled lake fish, sour shrimp, forest bamboo shoot, upland sticky rice, and roast suckling pig, with leaf-yeast wine when then singing is on. The Thái Nguyên portal adds grilled shrimp, pork over the fire, and khau nhuc. Five-colour sticky rice is the festival rice, and the only plate with a photograph. That photograph is the dish in Sơn La. The full list is on the food guide. A current price is Check on arrival. Book the meal and carry water. The hamlet has few shops.
interestsBody: The morning is the lake, with a boat at the landing. The same circuit takes you through Puong Cave and, if it is the long one, to Dau Dang. The night is the stilt-house floor at Pac Ngoi, not a bar street.

An Ma and Widow Island are landmarks on that boat. Fairy Pond is a look, and a park post forbids swimming. Hua Ma Cave is a walk on the south side. Tat Ma is a named fall in Dong Phuc. Cho Ra is the road town on the north edge.

interestGroups.title: Dining and F&B
interestGroups.summary: The meal is the Tay table in the stilt house: grilled lake fish, sour shrimp, upland sticky rice, and five-colour sticky rice.

cards.title: Dining and F&B
cards.summary: Five-colour sticky rice is the plate with a photograph, taken in Sơn La. The houses also cook grilled lake fish, sour shrimp, and bamboo-tube rice. A current price is Check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: The lake at breakfast
interestGroups.summary: For a morning on the water, with limestone on the walls and a boat at the landing.
body: Tay speakers call the widenings Slam Pe: Pe Leng, Pe Lu, and Pe Lam. The biodiversity desk says the water is one lake running nearly 8 km north–south. The park about page still says three lakes joined. You ride a boat. The usual circuit is the open water, An Ma, Fairy Pond, Puong, and Dau Dang, in combinations the boatman sells.

cards.title: Ba Be Lake
cards.summary: Green water, limestone, and the boats at the landing. Come for the morning. The fee is check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: The river cave and the fall
interestGroups.summary: For the boat that goes through Puong and lands at Dau Dang. They are one circuit.
body: Puong is on the Nang, about 1 km downstream from bến Buốc Lốm. The park page measures the cave at 300 m long, with a ceiling of 30–40 m. Dau Dang is about 3 km west of the lake. The park says the fall is about 53 m and that the slope of the stacked rock is estimated at 500 m. Do not read 500 m as a vertical drop.

cards.title: Puong Cave
cards.summary: Sit in the boat while it goes through. Footsteps, torchlight, and talking wake the bats. The fee is check on arrival.

cards.title: Dau Dang
cards.summary: White water on stacked rock, about 3 km west of the lake. The fish run is March and April. The fee is check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: Tay houses on the Leng
interestGroups.summary: For a night in a stilt house that faces the water, not a shop street.
body: Pac Ngoi is the Tay village on the Leng. VOV says nearly 100 stilt roofs, some a century old, and the hamlet head said about 80 percent of the old houses are still standing. VnExpress says about 40 nhân khẩu. Those two counts are not the same thing. The park counts Tay people at 57 percent of people living in the park, and Mong at 37 percent. After the meal, then singing and the đàn tính are the evening, if the house has called the hamlet troupe. A closing hour is check on arrival.

cards.title: Pac Ngoi
cards.summary: Stilt houses, the Leng, and the cliff. Sleep here so the boat is a morning. The stay is a homestay, not a sight ticket.

interestGroups.title: Limestone forest
interestGroups.summary: For the karst forest around the lake, and the walk the park actually clocks.
body: Both desks say the park is 10,048 ha. The about page, noting the old administrative units, splits that into strict protection 4,010.70 ha, ecological restoration 5,375.60 ha, admin-service 57.40 ha, and an inner buffer of 604.0 ha, plus an outer buffer of 25,309 ha. The biodiversity desk splits the same 10,048 ha into 3,846 ha strict, 6,162 ha restoration, and 40 ha admin. The walk with a clock is Keo Siu to An Ma, 5–6 hours, through forest the park calls primary. It says the walk is not a gentle outing.

cards.title: Ba Be National Park
cards.summary: Karst, forest, and the lake in one frame. The park is the whole trip, not a museum with one gate. The fee is check on arrival.

interestGroups.title: Islands in the water
interestGroups.summary: For the islands you pass on the boat. They are lake islands, not a sea crossing.
body: The about page names Widow Island and An Ma. Widow Island sits in Pe Leng. The park tells the story and describes stacked rock held by tree roots. It does not describe a landing pier. An Ma rises about 30 m, in a turtle-shell curve, and the temple is a Tay and Nung worship site.

cards.title: Islands in the lake
cards.summary: An island in the water, with the cliff behind.

season.label: Year round
season.note: The park describes two seasons, a northeast monsoon, a year-round mean of 22°C, about 1,378 mm of rain, and humidity above 80 percent. It does not print a road-closure calendar. VnExpress calls April–October the rainy season and November–February the dry season, says some places fall to 0°C with ice, and calls February–April the pleasant window at 25–30°C. That pleasant range and the freezing claim sit beside the park’s 22°C mean. March and April, after the first rains, are when the park says fish run Dau Dang. Mountain roads in a storm are check on arrival. Long Tong is the 10th of the first lunar month. The 2024 opening was 19 February and the 2026 opening was 26 February. The next civil date moves.

faqs.q: How big is Ba Be Lake?
faqs.a: The desks do not agree. The park about page: 150 m above sea level, 7.5 km long, depth 17–23 m, deepest 29 m. The biodiversity desk: about 178 m, length to 8 km, average depth 17–23 m, deepest about 35 m. UNESCO: 150 m, average depth 17–23 m, deepest 35 m. Lao Dong, citing the Thai Nguyen portal: 178 m, depth 17–29 m. VnExpress: 145 m, longer than 8 km, average depth 20 m, deepest 35 m.

faqs.q: Is Ba Be part of Cao Bang?
faqs.a: No. The lake is in Thái Nguyên after Resolution 202/2025/QH15 folded Bắc Kạn into that province. The park was under the Cao Bằng People’s Committee only from 1992 to 1997. Cao Bằng was not merged.

faqs.q: What does the park ticket cost?
faqs.a: Check on arrival. No park tariff was on the pages read. Operator sheets disagree with each other and were not used as the fee.
